_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Municipal-tier population-priority push, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18), round 17 of 20 (Wave D). Zambia — 22nd-highest-population country. `zm-zamstats-cpi` and `zm-social-cash-transfer-factsheet` already cover CPI/social protection; this round adds the council fiscal tier and the Local Government Equalisation Fund (LGEF). Important correction to a common assumption entering this round: the LGEF is NOT fixed at a specific percentage of national revenue by the Constitution — it is an annually-appropriated discretionary fund (Parliament decides the amount each year), with only its CAPITAL-EXPENDITURE portion (20%) fixed by statute.

reports.title: The Local Government Act, 2019 (No. 2 of 2019)
reports.description: Zambia's current local government law, verified via direct PDF download from parliament.gov.zm and pdftotext extraction. Sec. 25(1): a local authority "may make by-laws to impose a levy on" property owners/occupiers, businesses, or commodity sales within its area, with proceeds accruing to the authority (Sec. 25(3)). Sec. 27(1): power to impose fees/charges for licences, services, or goods supplied, subject to Ministerial approval for owners' rates and personal levy (Sec. 27(3)). Sec. 48: borrowing authority, subject to the Public Finance Management Act, 2018. Sec. 2 defines the "Equalisation Fund" as "the Local Government Equalisation Fund established under the Constitution" — a direct statutory cross-reference to the constitutional instrument. Sec. 47(1)-(4): the Minister of Finance may make regulations governing the Fund's administration; "A local authority shall use at least twenty percent of the funds received by a local authority from the Equalisation Fund, in any financial year, to finance capital expenditure"; an annual report on the Fund's operations must be laid before the National Assembly.

reports.title: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2016 — Article 163 (Local Government Equalisation Fund)
reports.description: Verified via direct PDF download. Art. 163(1): "There is established the Local Government Equalisation Fund." Art. 163(2): "Parliament shall annually appropriate monies to the Local Government Equalisation Fund which shall be disbursed by the Ministry responsible for finance to local authorities." Art. 163(3): "The Government may provide additional funds and grants to a local authority, as prescribed." IMPORTANT FINDING: this constitutional text does NOT fix the LGEF at 5% (or any fixed percentage) of national revenue — extensive search (this Constitution's full text, the repealed Local Government Act Cap. 281 which predates the LGEF entirely, and a 2016-vintage constitution mirror) found no primary Zambian legal text stating a fixed percentage currently in force. The Fund is discretionary annual parliamentary appropriation; only its capital-expenditure USE (20%, per zm-local-government-act-2019 Sec. 47(2)) is fixed by statute, not the total AMOUNT appropriated to it.

reports.title: Bi-Annual Budget Performance Review for Local Authorities for the Period Between 1st January to 30th June 2025
reports.publisher: Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development (MLGRD), Republic of Zambia, Department of Finance
reports.description: MLGRD's own semi-annual disbursement-performance report, verified directly. National LGEF disbursement performance H1 2025: "Disbursement was at 44%, with an additional 6% cleared in July, bringing the overall performance to 50%." Table 1 (Consolidated National Level): "Local Government Equalisation Fund [Budget] 1,444,004,186.24 [Actual] 724,952,406.35 [Performance] 50%." Provincial breakdowns given (not per-named-council): Eastern Province LGEF budget K166,728,827.87 / actual K74,429,229.20 / 45%; Lusaka Province budget K102,901,724.00 / actual K30,102,385.16 / 29%; Western Province budget K204,525,476.05 / actual K82,280,464.68 / 40%.
reports.cadence_note: Bi-annual budget performance review; this is the H1 2025 (January-June) edition, dated 22 September 2025.

reports.title: Report of the Committee on Local Government Accounts on the Report of the Auditor General on the Audit of Accounts of Local Authorities for the Financial Year Ended 31st December 2023
reports.publisher: National Assembly of Zambia (Committee on Local Government Accounts, drawing on Office of the Auditor General audits)
reports.description: The single strongest finding of this round — a national parliamentary committee reporting named, itemized, quantitative figures for individual city councils, verified via direct PDF download and pdftotext. Kitwe City Council (§28): over-collection of local revenue "K2,582,86[6]" broken down by category — "local taxes (K1,778,575), licenses (K249,834), levies (K2,360,958), permits (K1,071,577)" — and full utilization of its LGEF capital component: "Utilisation of Local Government Equalisation Fund – K4,663,674...the entire 20% capital component was spent on eligible projects including road maintenance, street lighting, and procurement of refuse equipment." Ndola City Council (§34): "the Council budgeted to receive funds amounting to K141,259,842 but only received K121,498,667, resulting in a funding shortfall of K19,761,175...total funds available stood at K138,577,713. Of this, K127,216,278 was expended, leaving a balance of K11,361,435 unspent." Lusaka City Council (§67): "budgeted to generate funds...totalling K443,059,301 against which amounts totalling K377,728,897, were received...an adverse variance of K65,330,404," and "Failure to Collect Property Rates K150,684,093...from 63,049 properties...with a ratable value of K75,386,465,135." National aggregate (§13, Treasury submission): "LAs had budgeted to receive grants from the MLGRD and to generate revenue from various sources, amounting to K3,765,372,879. However, the actual funds received and generated totaled K3,429,740,801." One council (Chiengi Town Council, §51) reported that a project "stalled due to the abolishment of the 20% capital component of the Equalisation Fund" — an internal tension with the still-in-force statutory 20% rule (Kitwe's own entry in the SAME report discusses full utilization of that same 20% component for the same fiscal year) — recorded as a documented ambiguity, not resolved.
reports.cadence_note: Annual parliamentary committee report on the Auditor-General's local-authority audit; this is the FY2023 edition.

dependencies.basis: The Act's own definitions section states directly: "'Equalisation Fund' means the Local Government Equalisation Fund established under the Constitution" (Sec. 2) — an explicit textual cross-reference from the statute to the constitutional instrument that creates the fund.

Kitwe City Council's own submission, as recorded in this report, directly invokes the statutory 20%-capital-expenditure rule: "the entire 20% capital component was spent on eligible projects" — the exact mechanism Sec. 47(2) of the Local Government Act, 2019 establishes.

The report repeatedly discusses named councils' receipt and use of the "Local Government Equalisation Fund (LGEF)" — the fund Article 163 of the Constitution establishes — including the Treasury's own submission committing to "continue to support LAs with the Local Government Equalisation Fund (LGEF)."

_dropped.edge: Lusaka City Council, Ndola City Council, Kitwe City Council -> own-published budget/financial-statement PDFs
_dropped.why: Real, specifically-titled documents were located via search for all three councils (e.g., Ndola's 'FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31st DECEMBER, 2024,' Kitwe's signed 2023 and 2024 financial statements, Lusaka's 'Approved 2025 Budget – Yellow Book') but NONE could be retrieved: lcc.gov.zm has an EXPIRED TLS certificate blocking all sub-paths; ndolacouncil.gov.zm and kitwecouncil.gov.zm both fail with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' (missing intermediate certificate chain). The same TLS-chain failure was independently confirmed on five additional smaller council domains (chipilicouncil.gov.zm, luangwacouncil.gov.zm, manyingacouncil.gov.zm, mbalacouncil.gov.zm) and on mofnp.gov.zm, suggesting a systemic hosting-layer misconfiguration across Zambian district/municipal government sites specifically — national-level domains (parliament.gov.zm, mlgrd.gov.zm) do not share this problem. Strong follow-up candidates once/if certificates are fixed.

_dropped.why: ZamStats' 'The Monthly' bulletin (May 2024 edition, directly verified) uses a 12-category CPI structure with names and ordering structurally identical to COICOP's 12 main divisions, but the bulletin text never uses the acronym 'COICOP,' never cites the IMF/ILO CPI Manual, and mentions SADC/COMESA only in unrelated trade-statistics tables elsewhere in the same bulletin, not in the CPI/inflation methodology section. _dropped.edge: Chiengi Town Council's claim that the LGEF's 20% capital component was 'abolished' -> a confirming legal/regulatory instrument
_dropped.why: One council submission within this same national report asserts the 20% capital component was abolished, while another council's entry in the identical report (Kitwe) discusses full utilization of that same 20% component for the same fiscal year. No separate primary legal instrument confirming a repeal of Local Government Act 2019 Sec. 47(2) was found — recorded as a genuine, unresolved internal inconsistency within a single primary document, not adjudicated either way.
